## 2

I understand why some images might seem questionable, especially when they come through media or edited photographs, but the evidence for a round Earth comes from far more than space photos. Ships disappear hull-first over the horizon, different stars are visible from different parts of Earth, time zones exist because sunlight reaches the curved surface at different angles, and lunar eclipses show Earth casting a consistently round shadow. Satellites, GPS, international flights, and observations made independently by countless scientists also rely on Earth being spherical. These different lines of evidence all agree, even without trusting any single photograph or agency.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of many colors. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny air molecules. Blue light gets scattered in all directions more strongly than most other colors, so blue light reaches our eyes from all across the sky. That is why the sky looks blue during the day. At sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere, which scatters away much of the blue before the light reaches us, leaving more reds and oranges.

雨下了一整夜，细密的水声敲打着窗玻璃，像有人在黑暗中轻轻叩门。街灯被雨幕晕染成昏黄的光团，积水映着屋檐和摇晃的树影，偶尔被驶过的汽车划开。远处传来模糊的鸣笛，转瞬又被雨声吞没。屋里很安静，只有钟表缓慢走动。我捧着一杯热茶站在窗前，看雨水顺着玻璃蜿蜒而下，仿佛整座城市都在这场夜雨中放慢了呼吸。
